on_screen_text.text: Vice President Harris on Republicans' anti-abortion agenda
Are you surprised at all at the raft of laws
that were quickly drafted after Roe v. Wade was overturned?
I think it's the height of irresponsibility
and in fact, in many cases, inhumane
We are looking at a situation where,
and again, as a former prosecutor, there would be no exception for rape or incest.
after a person has gone through a most vicious violation of their body—

and be able to make decisions about your body

spoken_summary: Stephen Colbert asks Kamala Harris if she is surprised by the anti-abortion laws passed after Roe v. Wade was overturned. Harris calls the laws the "height of irresponsibility" and "inhumane," highlighting that many have no exceptions for rape or incest. She passionately argues that after a "vicious violation" of their body, a person should not also have their autonomy taken away by the government. She concludes by stating that one does not need to abandon their faith to agree that "the government should not be telling her what to do with her body."
audio_music: The audio consists solely of spoken dialogue from an interview, followed by the sound of audience applause at the end.
editing_pacing: The editing consists of a single cut from the interviewer (Stephen Colbert) to the interviewee (Kamala Harris), who is then shown in a static talking-head shot for the rest of the clip.
cultural_references: The Late Show with Stephen Colbert
central_claim: Republican-backed anti-abortion laws are inhumane and irresponsible, as they strip individuals of bodily autonomy, even victims of rape and incest, which is an unacceptable overreach of government power.
intended_effect: To convince viewers that Republican policies on abortion are cruel and extreme, and to rally support for the Democratic position on protecting reproductive rights.
